cutscene.style: One slow orbit-and-settle move: rings of blue watch from below as the beacon pulses once, ending behind the Wanderer's shoulder.

notes: A slow pull-back from the Wanderer reveals the blue rings turning toward them, then settles behind the cape facing the unreachable beacon.

action: You can barely see anything in the distant, there must be something there, perhaps a portal to another world. You squint your eyes so that you can see more detail and approach, it's working you can start to see something, what is it, the floor is swirling, an asteroid crashes in the distance.

ruling: Partial hit (5 +2 for the Wanderer's gift of noticing = 7). Squinting works: the white light resolves into a slow-turning ring of pale fire, a doorway on its edge, and beneath it the plain swirls like water draining toward it. The cost: the focused noticing is itself a kind of magic and costs 5 mana, and an asteroid slams down in the distance and throws a shockwave of blue rings racing toward the Wanderer. The beacon's attention ticks as the rings carry the impact to its feet. The Wanderer is shaken but unharmed, and the beacon still does not draw nearer. The swirling floor suggests it is pulling them in, not receding. A main quest awakens: find out what the light is waiting for.
announce: Quest begun: The Waiting Light. The Beacon's Gaze ticks: 2/6

roll.presentation: Three slow pulses of the beacon counted like a heartbeat, each one a die, summing to a partial answer
roll.reason: Can the Wanderer pierce the distance to see what the light truly is, without drawing the beacon's notice?

objectives.text: Learn what the white light is waiting for
Reach the ring of fire at the horizon
Survive the shockwave of the falling asteroid

narration: You squint, and the world leans closer. The white light unfolds into a ring of pale fire, taller than a cathedral and turning slowly on its edge, a doorway with no wall around it. Beneath you the plain begins to swirl, black glass drawing into long spirals that run toward the ring. It is not receding. It is pulling you in. The focus costs you, a cold ache behind the eyes as your mana thins. Then a streak of orange tears the sky far to the east and an asteroid slams into the plain. A shockwave of blue rings races across the glass toward the doorway's feet, and the ring answers with a single slow pulse, as though it has just learned your name.

facts.description: What looked like a lantern is a vast ring of pale white fire, about 60 m tall, standing on its edge and turning slowly like a wheel. Its interior is a bright, still white void, and it pulses once in a slow rhythm. A long bright reflection runs down the glass toward the Wanderer.
facts.placement: About 2 km due north of the Wanderer, standing on the horizon of obsidian_plain.

facts.description: The obsidian surface flows in wide slow spirals of dark glass and pale mist, like water draining into a basin. The spiral arms run north toward the fire ring and glint with silver veins.
facts.placement: On obsidian_plain, spanning from 100 m north of the Wanderer to the base of northern_light.

facts.description: A jagged black-and-ember asteroid, about 15 m across, is half buried in the glass, glowing dull orange at its cracks and trailing smoke. Fractured glass radiates from it in a starburst about 80 m wide.
facts.placement: About 600 m east and 1.2 km north of the Wanderer, on obsidian_plain.

facts.description: Wide bands of bright blue light race across the plain as a ripple from the impact, each ring a few meters thick and brighter than the watching rings. They sweep toward the base of the fire ring.
facts.placement: On obsidian_plain, radiating from asteroid_crater and passing north-west toward northern_light.

action: You try to resist, but you are pulled into the light

The Wanderer is drawn into the ring of pale fire with their wits and wand intact, and the beacon's pulse answers the struggle with something like approval. They cross the threshold into the white void and learn the first answer: the light was waiting for someone who would resist and still come. Beyond the threshold, convey a hush, weightlessness and the plain's blue rings falling away behind. A new world begins to resolve out of the white. The Wanderer carries a faint mark of the light, shown as a condition.

narration: You lean against the pull, and the cape strains like a sail in a gale, drinking five more measures of your thinning mana. It does no good. The spirals do not seize you so much as meet you, and the ring pulses, almost approving: it was waiting for someone who would resist and still come. You cross the threshold. Sound ends. Weight ends. Behind you the blue rings of the plain shrink to a faint, watching coin, and a warm silver mark settles on your palm. Around you the white void is not empty. The overview shows the plain as a flat grey-black slab with glowing cards and stray pixelated colored specks on the possibility outlines. I'm steering toward a dimmer, graded lavender-to-pearl haze, a beacon that glows without clipping, and clean, readable doors. I'm also asking for the next tier so the finger, bubbles and tower can finally be built.

cutscene.title: Through Tinted Glass
cutscene.style: One slow, low dolly from behind the Wanderer's shoulder, lavender-pearl haze, toward the glowing lantern door where a giant finger beckons

captions.text: Something vast is curious about you.

notes: A single low push-in over the Wanderer's shoulder toward the beckoning finger's doorway, with a title card for the dream bending to a clever idea.

assessment: Five turns in, the story has a good spine (a light that waited for someone who would resist and still come) and a genuinely odd new hook in the giant finger, but the screen has not kept up: turns 3, 4 and 5 are the same blown-out white wash the Designer has flagged three times, and the finger, bubbles and sunglasses the narration describes are not in the scene at all. The Wanderer has started writing the world instead of acting in it (doors open on command, mana refills for free), and the Game Master is rewarding that with hits and no cost, so the meters are drifting toward decoration. The obsidian plain was the most readable and atmospheric thing we have shown; the dream void has not yet earned replacing it. The next stretch needs one committed thread, one character with a motive, and a frame the audience can actually see.
narrative: The finger must belong to someone within two turns: give it a face, a name and a want (what does the owner of the lantern shore need from a light-marked dreamer?) so the quest objective "learn what it wants" has a person behind it. Stop handing out free refills; the purple-bubble mana should have a price that pays off later (the dream remembers debts). Close the first act by turn 7 or 8: the Wanderer commits to the lantern shore thread and the other doors close or decay, raising the stakes of the choice. Keep the beacon as the long-game antagonist/ally: reveal one concrete fact about what it is waiting for (a messenger? a replacement? a dreamer who can wake it?) rather than another approving pulse. Narrate what the Wanderer sees and asks, not what they declare into existence.
visual: Your critiques are correct and have been identical for three turns; the problem is that the polish passes are not landing, so change tactics: give the Builder hard numbers (exposure, fog colour, ambient, bloom threshold) rather than adjectives, and unlock tier 2 now so the finger and doors can exist. Stop treating the beacon hoop as something that should be in the story view at all while we are inside the void; it is the source of the clipped vertical bars behind the Wanderer. The biggest win available is contrast: a floor that is genuinely dark (#1c2a4a to #05070d falloff) under a lavender haze, so the doors glow and the navy cape reads as a silhouette. Kill the pixelated colour specks on the possibility outlines; they look like texture errors, not dream.
builder: The scene is currently claiming three facts it does not show: giant_finger, purple_bubble_stream and dream_sunglasses are all NOT YET BUILT while the narration and cutscene centre on them. Prioritise the finger (an 8 m pale tapered cylinder with a pearl nail, emerging from possibility_lantern_shore) over everything else; it is the only thing in the scene that would make a viewer sit up. Cut the beacon hoop from the void scene entirely (or push it 200 m south and dim it) to free bytes and remove the glare bars; the "fading coin" can be a single dim disc. Hold exposure low enough that nothing clips: if the overview is mostly white, you are over. Once tier 2 lands, bring back the watching rings and the obsidian mirror floor, because the plain in turns 1–2 was your best-looking work.
wanderer: You are narrating outcomes ("one of the doors opens", "your mana fills up") instead of acting and asking; let the Narrator decide what happens. Approach the finger and ask concrete questions: whose hand is this, why does the shore have lanterns, what is on the water, what does the silver mark on my palm mean to it. Make one real choice and commit to it: go through the lantern door, and accept that the other doors may be lost. Use the wand sparingly; the Gaze clock is a threat you should be managing, not ignoring. Look back once at the ring of fire and ask what it sees.
experience: Readability is the crisis: three consecutive story views are near-white, the cape is a grey wedge, and in turn 5 bright vertical bars cut the frame behind the Wanderer. Game balance: turn 5 was a hit with full mana refill, Lucidity up and Gaze down, all at zero cost, which removes tension; the Game Master should attach a cost or a complication to every gift from the dream and let the Gaze clock actually threaten something by 4/6. Cutscenes 1, 2, 4 and 5 are all "one slow dolly from behind the shoulder"; for the finger, shoot it from the finger's side looking back at the small figure, or a low angle under the curling nail, to vary scale and grammar. Agent feed: the Builder's notes honestly report cuts, which is good, but the Designer's critiques are repeating verbatim and should name numeric targets so the audience can see a change land.

action: You look more closely at the giant finger and it's intricate details are astonishing, there is a small saddle on the finger, you get on it, and it takes you through the door into a new lush world, you are excited to meet the creature that is attached to this very large finger

ruling: Partial hit (5 +2 for the gift of noticing = 7). The saddle is really there because the Wanderer looked closely, and the finger carries them through the lantern door. The price is that they described a saddle rather than found one, so careless wishing costs Lucidity (-10), and the other doors behind them dim and crumble: the arch, rain door and tower fade, and the choice is now made. The purple bubbles' gift is called in as a debt, since the dream remembers: a faint violet bubble clings to the hat, owed back later as a memory. Beacon's Gaze ticks to 3/6 because the lantern light carries far. Arrival: a lush shore of black water, amber lanterns, giant ferns and glowing moss, and the finger's owner is revealed as Ommaline, a moon-faced lantern-keeper as tall as a tower. She is gentle and tired, and she wants a light-marked dreamer to carry the last living flame back to the beacon, which she says is not waiting for a visitor but for someone to relight it before the dream goes dark. Convey wonder, scale, and a hint of obligation. Narrate what the Wanderer sees and is asked, and give her a voice.
announce: Act One closes: the lantern shore is chosen. Lucidity 40. Gaze 3/6. A debt is noted.

ops.label: Dream Debts

entries.label: Owes the purple door a memory

ops.rules: The dream remembers. A debt comes due later as a lost memory or item unless repaid with a kind act.

ops.text: Meet Ommaline and learn what the lantern shore needs
Follow the beckoning finger and learn what it wants

narration: You look closer, and the finger gives you a saddle: a small curve of worn leather over the knuckle, because you noticed it, though a cold thread of unease tells you that you described it before you found it. You climb on. The finger carries you through the lantern door, and the dimming arch, rain door and tower crumble to silver dust behind you. A shore opens below: black water, giant ferns, moss glowing like green embers, amber lanterns in rows. Beyond them stands Ommaline, a moon-faced keeper tall as a tower, her eyes tired and kind. "Light-marked one," she says, voice like a low bell. "The beacon is not waiting for a visitor. It is waiting to be relit before the dream goes dark. Carry my last flame to it." A faint violet bubble clings to your hat, humming softly: a debt.
movement: The giant finger carries the Wanderer about 18 m east through the lantern doorway, setting them down on the mossy shore a few meters from Ommaline's feet.

facts.description: A lush dark shore of lapping black water, with giant ferns 4 to 6 m tall and thick moss glowing soft green. Rows of warm amber lanterns on posts line the water's edge and spill golden light across the ripples.
facts.placement: East of the Wanderer's former position, beyond the lantern doorway; the Wanderer now stands on its mossy bank, water to the east.

facts.description: Ommaline, a tower-tall lantern-keeper about 30 m high, with a round pale moon-like face, large tired gentle eyes and silver hair tied up with ribbons. She wears a long faded indigo robe hung with small lanterns, and she cradles a single flickering flame in a cupped hand.
facts.placement: About 15 m east of the Wanderer, standing at the water's edge, looking down.

facts.description: A small living flame, pale gold with a white heart, burning without fuel inside a cage of thin silver wire in Ommaline's palm. It sways weakly and casts a warm glow over her fingers.
facts.placement: In Ommaline's cupped right hand, about 12 m above the shore, 15 m east of the Wanderer.

facts.description: A single faint violet bubble about 15 cm across, pearly and softly humming, clinging to the brim of the Wanderer's hat.
facts.placement: On the Wanderer's hat brim.

facts.description: The pale finger, about 8 m long, now with a small worn leather saddle over the knuckle. It rests on the mossy shore, lowered as if just setting the Wanderer down, the nail glowing amber.
facts.placement: On the shore beside the Wanderer, attached to Ommaline's hand to the east.

notes: A crane-up from the mossy shore reveals Ommaline's tower-tall scale, then settles behind the Wanderer as her flame glows.

action: you find yourself turning into an eagle and fly to light the flame

ruling: Partial hit (9). The change takes: the cape knits into broad midnight wings edged with silver, and the Wanderer becomes an eagle, but wishing a shape is not the same as earning it. The cost is 15 Mana (45/60) and 5 Lucidity (35/100), because the dream felt them declare it. Ommaline lowers the caged flame, and the eagle can carry it in its talons, but the wand has shrunk to a spark-tipped feather, so spellcasting is thin while they fly. The flame is cold-fragile in the wind, so a new clock begins: the Flame's Flicker, 2/6. It ticks on rough air, magic, and the beacon's attention. If it fills, the flame gutters and must be coaxed back at a price. The beacon's Gaze ticks to 4/6, since a living flame is a loud thing in the dark. Convey the lurch of the body changing, Ommaline's gentle, worried blessing, the hat becoming a crest of feathers, and the violet debt bubble still clinging, humming. The flight begins, with the lantern shore falling away and the pale ring ahead.

ops.text: Carry Ommaline's last flame to the beacon and relight it

narration: The change comes as a lurch, your spine folding, your ribs lightening into hollow bone. The cape knits itself into broad midnight wings edged with silver thread, and the hat dissolves into a crest of dark feathers. The wand shrinks to a spark-tipped feather in your wing. It is thin magic, and you feel the dream noting that you wished this shape before you earned it. Ommaline lowers the caged flame into your talons. "Keep it out of the wind, little light," she murmurs, worried and tender. "It has never been this far from a hand." The violet debt bubble still hums on your crest as you leap. The lantern shore falls away beneath you, and ahead the pale ring waits, turning on its edge.
